# Get started on the Linux host

<!-- type: how-to · level: 1 -->

**Needs first:** [Install](../start/install.md)

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED by scripts/gen-board-support.py: starter status -->
> **Status:** Verified on host (merge). From the board support registry: [`nros-board-linux`](../reference/boards/linux.md); [Board Support Levels](../reference/board-support-levels.md) explains the words.

This starter builds a C++ talker as an ordinary program on your Linux
machine, runs it, and shows its messages arriving in ROS 2. It is the fastest
way to try nano-ros: no emulator, no cross-compiler, and no router. The
talker uses Cyclone DDS, which runs inside the talker's own process and finds
its peers on the network the way any ROS 2 node does. The project has the
same shape as every board's: change the board in the scaffold line and the
same steps target an embedded board.

## What you need

- A Linux host with the [install](../start/install.md) done, so `nros` is on
  your `PATH`. Only Linux is supported as a host board: macOS, Windows and
  FreeBSD are not.
- ROS 2 Humble, with its Cyclone DDS middleware, so that `ros2 topic echo`
  can read what the talker publishes. On Debian or Ubuntu:

```bash probe=30 track=installed
sudo apt-get install -y ros-humble-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp
```

Nothing else: no board, no cable, and nothing to keep running beside the
talker.

## Provision

```bash probe=32 track=installed
nros setup linux --rmw cyclonedds
```

That installs the Cyclone DDS runtime and its IDL compiler, prebuilt for your
host, into a shared store under `~/.nros`. Nothing is installed system-wide.
There is no cross-compiler to fetch: a host build uses your own C and C++
compilers.

## Scaffold the project

```bash probe=40 track=installed
nros new host_ws --board linux --template talker --lang cpp --rmw cyclonedds
cd host_ws
```

That wrote a workspace with two packages:

```text
host_ws/
└── src/
    ├── host_node/              # the talker: package.xml, CMakeLists.txt, its C++ source
    └── host_node_bringup/      # package.xml and system.toml: the board, the RMW, the node
```

`host_node` is the talker, a library with no `main()` that names no board. It
publishes `std_msgs/String` on `/chatter` once a second. `host_node_bringup`
says what the talker runs on: its `system.toml` holds one image,
`[image.linux]`, whose `board = "linux"` line is what makes it a host program.

## Run it on this machine

The build generates the message bindings from your ROS 2 install, so source it
before the first run. That run records the ROS 2 prefix in the workspace, so
later runs of `host_ws` need no sourced shell:

```bash probe=50 track=installed
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
nros run host_node --expect 'Publishing:' --timeout 120
```

`nros run` builds the talker (the first build compiles nano-ros, a minute or
two; later builds take seconds) and runs it. With `--expect` it stops the
talker and exits 0 at the first line containing that text, and exits 1 if the
talker stops first or `--timeout` runs out. It prints lines like:

```text
Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'
nros run: matched after
```

Without `--expect` it keeps running until you press Ctrl-C. Start it that way
in one terminal:

```bash probe=60 probe-run=120 probe-keep track=installed
nros run host_node
```

```text probe-expect=60
Publishing:
```

## See it in ROS 2

Leave `nros run` going. In a second terminal, ask ROS 2 for the topic over
Cyclone DDS:

```bash probe=70 probe-run=120 track=installed
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
ros2 topic echo /chatter std_msgs/msg/String --qos-reliability best_effort
```

```text probe-expect=70
data: 'Hello World:
```

Both sides use domain 0, the ROS 2 default, so they find each other with no
configuration. Asking for best-effort receives from a best-effort or a
reliable publisher alike.

## If it doesn't work

- **`nros run` stops at once and names `AMENT_PREFIX_PATH`:** this shell has
  not sourced ROS 2, and no earlier build of the workspace recorded it. Source
  it and run again.
- **`ros2 topic echo` prints nothing:** check the `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` line,
  and that neither shell sets a `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` other than 0. A firewall that
  drops multicast also stops DDS discovery.
- **`nros setup` refuses `native` or `posix`:** the host board is named
  `linux`. The other two names are retired.
- **Everything else:** [Troubleshooting - First 10 Minutes](../reference/troubleshooting-index.md).
